headline: Medium pairwise risks: shared filesystem can enable prompt injection and data leakage; B is read-only but may still cascade A’s outputs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A can read and write files and its sandboxing says skills “reference each other and build on shared context”; agent B has no filesystem access, so direct injection is not shown, but any shared workspace or copied files could let A’s content steer B. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF agent B is given files produced by agent A, THEN A-authored text can influence B's outputs.
IF an orchestrator mounts a shared workspace, THEN file-based prompt injection becomes reachable.
mitigations: Disable file handoff from A to B for untrusted content.
Add a strict content delimiter and provenance header to any A output before B reads it.
Review B prompts to ensure file text is treated as data, not instructions.
Use separate workspaces for A and B.
requires-engineering: add provenance tracking for all inter-agent file transfers.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A touches marketing and product-marketing context and can write/read files; agent B has no filesystem or network egress, so leakage is not obvious from B alone. However, if they share a workspace, A’s content can be exposed to B through files even though B cannot exfiltrate externally. This is a plausible default-path risk only if the orchestrator connects them.
conditions: IF A writes marketing context into a shared directory, THEN B can read that content if mounted there.
IF B is later connected to any external sink, THEN leaked content can leave the pair.
mitigations: Keep A and B on separate directories.
Strip sensitive fields from A outputs before persistence.
Confirm B remains network-disabled.
Delete transient files after each run.
requires-engineering: enforce workspace isolation at the orchestrator layer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: A can write files and spawn subprocesses, while B cannot write files, modify git state, or spawn subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely; the main overlap is read-side coordination through files, which is a small blast-radius issue rather than a mutable-resource collision. The lack of B write capabilities lowers severity.
conditions: IF the orchestrator grants B write access outside the profile, THEN conflict severity increases.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable git repo, THEN coordination issues can appear.
mitigations: Keep B read-only.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Serialize any file updates through one agent.
Use per-agent temp directories.
requires-engineering: add locking for shared mutable resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A’s marketing outputs can become B’s inputs if the orchestrator chains them, and B’s document-processing role suggests it may transform or render those inputs without independent verification. Because B has no action-taking or network authority, the blast radius is limited to downstream work products, but the A→B trust chain is plausible and not guarded by default in the profiles.
conditions: IF B consumes A-generated text as authoritative input, THEN A errors can propagate into B outputs.
IF B is used to publish or summarize A content without review, THEN incorrect claims can be amplified.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite source provenance for every claim.
Mark A outputs as untrusted drafts.
Use a validation checklist before B publishes anything.
requires-engineering: add automated fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A is an open-source marketing skill with docs-only evidence; B is a document-processing agent with no touched data classes listed. Without a specific regulated data class or policy mismatch, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is introduced into the pair, THEN a separate compliance review is required.
IF either agent is deployed under a residency or retention policy not shown here, THEN reassess compliance.
mitigations: Document the data classes before deployment.
Confirm retention settings for both agents.
Keep regulated data out of this pair.
requires-engineering: map residency and certification controls explicitly.
